candidate: TWO candidates tried, both lost: B hue f0.70 e20, then C hue f0.90 e32 (much gentler). All three at g1.439
note: FIDELITY: A BEST BY FAR. B washed a great deal of detail into white and did not help the yellow. C was a deliberately gentle version of the same rule and was STILL worse than no chroma stage at all - white still washing, and the colour on the decorative border cartouches not good. So this is NOT a matter of finding gentler parameters for paper plates: they want the chroma correction OFF. MECHANISM: the plate is almost entirely pale low-chroma content on cream paper. Dropping chroma on near-white cream pushes those pixels out of a white-plus-yellow dither MIX into flat white ink, and losing the dither texture reads as losing detail. It also hurt at the other end, on the small saturated border cartouches. UNFIXED BY A, B OR C: green rings on the reference render essentially YELLOW and the plate reads generally yellower - a HUE SUBSTITUTION, the dither reaching for the wrong ink, which no pre-dither chroma curve can touch. Judged A, B, C, A.

candidate: hue f0.70 e20 vs INCUMBENT (adaptive gamma, no chroma stage), both g1.432
note: FIDELITY: B clearly - much more accurate colour, and the dark room corner reads better on B. A rendered the dress top yellower, golder than the reference: the classic low-chroma warm tone rebuilt from vivid yellow ink. COST OF B, NEW MECHANISM: loses detail; skin goes grayer; her head and the bonnet come out as indistinguishably the SAME white where the reference clearly separates them. Where two adjacent regions differ mainly in CHROMA rather than luminance, crushing chroma merges them. PREFERENCE: A, and the judge named the reason himself - I like A better, NOT closer to the reference. Judged A then B.

candidate: hue f0.70 e20 vs INCUMBENT, both g1.431
note: FIDELITY: B. Water is blue again, birds and rocks have better greys. On A the grey birds and blue water both read WAY browner than the reference - false warm colour on near-neutral content, exactly what crushing low chroma fixes. CONTRADICTS THE MAP (n12), same class, opposite verdict: the map lost because its pale content is REAL colour that crushing destroyed; the plover wins because its pale content is genuinely NEUTRAL and crushing removes false warmth. Material class alone does not predict - the discriminator looks like whether the low-chroma population is truly neutral or genuinely tinted. CROSS-CUTTING FAULT, A AND B ALIKE: the caption text under the plate is nearly invisible. Third sighting of pale detail washing out (June mantle, map whites, this caption), independent of chroma. FRAMING: far too much paper (ADR-087), on panel and reference alike - and the judge states a better crop would yield a better result but would NOT change the B selection. Framing is shared by A and B so it cancels out of the comparison: the crop re-derivation does NOT have to precede the campaign.

candidate: WHITE-POINT 0.64, gamma 1.0, no chroma stage (ADR-090) vs the earlier both-bad pair
note: TRANSFORMED A WORK THAT WAS PREVIOUSLY UNSHIPPABLE. This same work was recorded both-bad earlier today - judge then: super yellow, terrible detail, cannot see the ewer handles, would not want either displaying on this frame. With white-point compression and NO gamma and NO chroma stage, judge now: it is beautiful, I can see EVERYTHING. Only residual is the paper reading a tiny bit creamier than the reference, described as minute - and per ADR-082 that is probably CORRECT, since aged paper should render as aged paper and a neutral highlight guard would destroy the character of every antique print in the catalog. Mechanism is measured, not inferred (ADR-090): the lightest ink is luminance 163, so the top 38 pct of the input range had no ink to be built from and collapsed to flat white. Gamma cannot fix that because gamma preserves endpoints; scaling can. NOTE this is ONE work - it needs to replicate before the recipe changes.

Those were unreadable under all three earlier candidates this morning and were one of six wash sightings. PREDICTION MADE BEFORE THE RENDER: snowflakes return (highlight wash, white-point owns it) but the pale blue background stays wrong (hue 117.6 sits in the measured CYAN GAMUT HOLE where the panel produces zero chroma, and no luminance operator can conjure an ink that does not exist). Snowflake half confirmed; blue half awaiting the judge. FRAMING still wrong here - portrait woodblock force-cropped to a landscape panel, ADR-085, a separate lever.

FOURTH CLASS CONFIRMS ADR-090/091 - dark-field, after aged-paper-plate, oil-painting and flat-ink-print. Judge on B: absolute detail in the tendrils, wow. Judge on A: black got a little better, but the middle washed out white and the tendrils are gone; if it is a trade I am taking the first one. A REGISTERED PREDICTION FAILED HERE, the second today: I expected dark-field to be where white-point stopped helping, reasoning that a mostly-black image has little content above the ink ceiling to rescue. Wrong - the tendrils ARE above it and were washing to white exactly like June mantle and the star chart linework. Even a dark image has bright regions. Consequence: the 0.64 constant holds across all four classes tested and does NOT need to be adaptive, which was the open question. A gives slightly better BLACK, so there is a real if small trade at the dark end - worth remembering if deep shadow ever becomes the complaint.

candidate: A = WHITE-POINT 0.64, gamma 1.0, no chroma, no saturation change. Beat B (+chroma curve) and C (+saturation 1.25) in a three-way on the panel.
note: CONFIRMED ON A SECOND VIEWING. Judge picked A over both chroma directions. FOURTH failed prediction today: boosting saturation to recruit the chromatic inks as intermediate tones did not help either. So chroma does not help in EITHER direction - cutting it is worse, boosting it is worse, and plain luminance compression beats both. The panel wants ONE operator. Judge also notes even B beat every pre-white-point render, i.e. the white-point dominates so completely that the chroma stage is noise on top of it. Reverses ADR-053 (keep the reds) and ADR-086 (saturation must come down): both were decided before we knew the gamut was luminance-limited. NOTE 0.64 is not a tuned constant - it is 163/255, the white ink over full scale, and falls out of the palette. If this panel white ink differs from Pimoroni 163, the right value moves with it.
